tagline: Complete Operations, explicit Specs and bounded execution.
title: Concorde Framework

homepage.eyebrow: Complete Operations · Explicit Specs · Bounded execution
homepage.title: Specify responsibilities. Compose Operations.
homepage.description: Concorde provides complete Operations for understanding software, preparing contracts and developing verified changes. Modules own responsibilities and Specs; LangGraph graphs compose executable behavior. Trusted Host and Harness services enforce each task's context and permission boundaries.

items.title: Read complete Module specifications.
items.description: Module Specs explain purpose, terminology, correct use, design and relationships. Implementation Specs define precise requirements, scenarios and contracts. Both belong to one Module, with paired reading and metadata sources and explicit context references.

items.title: Call complete Operations.
items.description: An Operation declares input State, output updates, effects, use conditions and execution policy. Callers do not reconstruct context selection, permission boundaries, model execution or result checks to use it as a LangGraph node.

items.title: Keep authority outside State.
items.description: Completeness still relies on trusted Runtime, Host and Harness services. Operations declare permission ceilings; the common Host and Harness narrow and enforce them for the actual task. State cannot carry or expand execution authority.

items.title: Compose without confusing ownership.
items.description: Deterministic code, model execution and compiled graphs can implement Operations. Composition produces another Operation, including dev-loop and specify-loop. Module ownership, Operation composition and context references remain independent.

items.title: Retain evidence and explicit stopping conditions.
items.description: Missing contracts, failed checks and incomplete reviews remain inspectable. Evidence binds to the exact inputs checked. A ready candidate is not a merge; delivery and any primary merge require separate authorization.

workflow.title: Choose the result you need.
workflow.description: Use main for a question or routing, specify-loop for an independently reviewed contract, and dev-loop for a verified development candidate. Public/internal changes entry exposure, not an Operation's completeness.

steps.title: Route & specify
steps.description: Select the responsible Module, establish its contract and review the Spec.

steps.title: Plan & implement
steps.description: Turn the contract into tasks, then write code within the declared file grant.

steps.title: Validate & review
steps.description: Run deterministic checks and independent review against current inputs.

steps.title: Ready, not merged
steps.description: Inspect the candidate. Request delivery separately; merging primary needs additional authorization.

quickstart.title: Start with an explicit project contract.
quickstart.description: Clone and build Concorde, then preview installation into your Git project. Use Python 3.11+, Node.js 18+ and npm; configured checks require Linux with bubblewrap, working namespaces and pidfd support. Choose Codex or Claude for the public Skills; model-backed Operations execute through Pi workers.
quickstart.code:
git clone https://github.com/FTOD/concorde.git
cd concorde
python3 scripts/concorde.py build

# Replace the path with your Git project.
python3 scripts/install-concorde.py \
  --target /absolute/path/to/project \
  --integration codex --preview

# Review the preview, then rerun with --apply.

reference.title: Operations and executable entry points
reference.description: The checked inventory contains 26 Operations: 14 host adapters and 12 model-backed internal Operations. Nine public Operations have Skills; four public lifecycle entries make no model calls. A Module can own several Operations, and a composed Operation can use several provider Modules.

tables.title: Public Operations
tables.description: Every public entry uses the common admission boundary. Internal Operations remain complete building blocks available only to admitted compositions.
rows: concorde-main
Answer a question, route a task or propose and apply explicitly accepted topology.
concorde-specify-loop
Compose Spec authoring and independent review, stopping before planning and implementation.
concorde-dev-loop
Compose specification, planning, implementation and verification to a ready candidate, not a merge.
concorde-review
Return scoped, independent Spec or code review findings without starting a development change.
concorde-issues
Inspect, report, reopen or solve an explicit Issue; solving stops at a verified candidate.
concorde-init
Propose and apply initialization with a pinned Protocol and an honest Module stub.
concorde-configure
Apply explicit Pi worker model, thinking and timeout settings; accept an installed Protocol only when requested.
concorde-validate
Record current deterministic validation evidence for a candidate.
concorde-deliver
Publish a verified delivery branch and normally remove its source worktree; merge primary only on a separate request.

tables.title: Model-backed Operations
tables.description: These are Operations with model execution profiles, not a second executable entity inventory. Each bounded worker is a fresh Pi execution with host-issued context, tools and limits.
rows: answerer, router, topology-designer
Reason from explicitly selected complete Module Specs without implementation contents.
spec-author, topology-author, spec-reviewer
Author owner-only proposals or perform independent read-only review; the Host validates and applies admitted changes.
context-assessor, planner, task-author
Assess contract sufficiency and produce plans and acceptance tasks without reading implementation contents.
programmer, code-reviewer, issue-solver
Implement within the file grant, review code read-only, or choose bounded Issue resolution. Only the implementation phase receives project write authority.

tables.title: Shared execution services
tables.description: The Operations hierarchy groups behavior providers, including composed providers. Supporting Modules own their separate contracts; using them neither transfers ownership nor expands context references.
rows: Development
Admit public requests and enforce declared Operation composition through the common Host.
Harness
Prepare bounded model execution, narrow permissions and validate worker results.
Spec
Resolve stable identities, complete paired document units and explicit context selections.
Distribution, Issues, Views
Supply fresh assets, retain attributed problems and publish contracts and inspection views.

tables.title: Launchers and supporting tools
tables.description: Source-checkout commands are shown below. Installed projects use the corresponding scripts under .concorde/framework/. Direct CLI validation is distinct from lifecycle readiness evidence.
rows: python3 scripts/run-operation.py <skill> < invocation.json
Submit a typed request for one of the nine public Operations.
python3 scripts/concorde.py <command>
Build, validate, publish documentation, inspect usage or explicitly refresh Protocol bindings.
LangGraph Studio
Inspect and execute the same admitted public graphs as the CLI and Skills.
python3 scripts/install-concorde.py
Preview or apply installation into a project.
python3 scripts/issues.py
Inspect Issues or explicitly archive historical Reflection records.
npm --prefix docsite run <script>
Start, build, validate, typecheck or test the documentation site.
python3 scripts/development/run-tests.py
Run deterministic Python tests without starting Concorde's development graphs.
